Works with

Rugged tablet for ShireSystem (formerly Pirana CMMS)

ShireSystem is the computerised maintenance management system that Shire Systems of Southampton sold for years as Pirana CMMS. Trade press from 2016 describes Pirana's Work Orders PRO and Data Collector PRO mobile apps, and the Android app on Google Play still carries the package name co.uk.shiresystems.pirana, but the product is now sold by Elecosoft UK Ltd, trading as Eleco, as ShireSystem. The vendor's product page describes it as a CMMS that helps you take control of your assets, plan maintenance efficiently, and reduce unplanned downtime, used across the aviation, automotive, healthcare, education, food and drink manufacturing, industrial and retail sectors, with four plans (Essentials, Professional, Advanced and Expert) priced on quote. The main system runs in a browser, either as Eleco's cloud service or on a customer's own Windows server.

On the floor, engineers use ShireSystem Mobile Pro. The vendor's Mobile Pro page says mobile users have access to a wealth of work order information including documents, parts, labour costs, meter readings and images, that job sign-off can be initiated by optionally scanning a barcode and can require customer, engineer and a third signature, that the Data Collector creates new assets, movements and locations, and that stock items can be received into stores, stocktakes performed and parts issued to work orders. The Google Play listing sums it up as Work Orders, Materials and Data Collection, use on or offline. That work happens in plant rooms, food factories, depots and estates, where a consumer phone in a case tends to run flat, crack or fog up.

This page sets out what Eleco publishes about the devices the app and the browser client run on, what it does not publish, which Tuga rugged devices meet the published figures, and how a UK maintenance team can buy one trial unit before standardising. Nothing here is a vendor endorsement: ShireSystem has not been tested on Tuga devices by either company, so check your own account on the device during the 30-day returns window.

Requirements

What ShireSystem (formerly Pirana CMMS) and the Mobile Pro app needs from a device

Each item below comes from Elecosoft UK Ltd, trading as Eleco's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 4.1 or later, from Google Play, published as a phone app

    ShireSystem Mobile PRO is on Google Play from developer Elecosoft (package co.uk.shiresystems.pirana). When read on 25 October 2026 the listing showed version 4.1.0.8, updated 15 September 2025, with the release note Fixes scrolling issue on the Subject Info page, a minimum API level of 16 (Android 4.1) and a target API level of 34 in the listing data, a Phone device chip and no Tablet chip, and a rating of 3.3 stars. The minimum is low enough that every Tuga Android device clears it by many versions; the absence of a Tablet chip means Google Play may describe the app as designed for phones on a tablet, which is a reason to trial it on the device you intend to buy. Source: play.google.com

  • A current ShireSystem licence and software version 3.2.6 or later

    The vendor's Mobile Pro page says the app is available providing you have purchased relevant licences and are on ShireSystem software version 3.2.6 or later, and links to the Google Play and App Store listings. Mobile Pro is a companion to a ShireSystem account, not a standalone product, so this page is for teams that already run ShireSystem and now need devices for the engineers. Source: elecosoft.com

  • Browser client: the latest version of an industry standard browser, Chrome recommended

    Eleco's system requirements guide says ShireSystem, cloud or on premise, is accessed through the latest version of an industry standard web browser, with Google Chrome recommended and Microsoft Edge and Mozilla Firefox also supported, or through iOS and Android mobile apps. It gives no minimum Android or iOS version and no device specification for the apps. The same guide lists the on-premise server requirements (Windows Server 2016 to 2022, a 64-bit dual-core 2GHz processor, 16GB RAM and 100GB free disk for 3 to 20 concurrent users, IIS, SQL Server) which apply to the server, not to the devices engineers carry. Source: help.elecosoft.com

  • Works on or offline

    The Google Play description says use on or offline, and the App Store listing for the iOS version says teams can track and maintain assets both online and offline. Neither listing nor the requirements guide says how much data the app caches on the device or how sync conflicts are handled, so test a plant room with no signal during the trial. Source: apps.apple.com

  • QR codes, barcodes and RFID tags for sign-off, assets and stock

    The Mobile Pro page says QR, Barcodes and RDIF tags are also supported (the page's own spelling) and that job sign-off can be initiated by optionally scanning a barcode. The App Store release notes add that Part Code and Store can be set with one QR code scan and that work orders can be started and finished by scanning a barcode. The vendor does not say whether scanning uses the camera, a built-in scan engine or a Bluetooth scanner, or which RFID frequency it means, so check the method your administrator has configured. Source: elecosoft.com

  • Network: 10 Mbps download and 5 Mbps upload recommended

    The requirements guide recommends a minimum download speed of 10 Mbps and a minimum upload speed of 5 Mbps for best performance. It is written for the browser client, but it is a fair target for a 4G tablet uploading work order photos from site. Source: help.elecosoft.com

  • RAM, storage and screen size: not published

    No minimum or recommended RAM, storage or screen size for Mobile Pro was found on the Google Play listing, the Mobile Pro page or the requirements guide when read on 25 October 2026. The iOS version of the app lists iOS 11.0 or later and is designed for iPad, which suggests tablet layouts exist on that platform; on Android, Google Play shows only a Phone chip. If your Eleco account manager gives a device specification, check it against the figures below. Source: play.google.com

  • Stay on a supported release

    The requirements guide says Eleco shall maintain technical support on the two most current releases of the software. The App Store notes say Entra ID single sign-on and the latest Document Manager need ShireSystem V4.5 onward, so a team on an old ShireSystem release may find the current app expects features its server does not have. Keep the server, the app and the device's Android updates current together. Source: help.elecosoft.com

Setting up

Getting ShireSystem (formerly Pirana CMMS) and the Mobile Pro app running

  1. Ask your ShireSystem administrator to confirm the account is on version 3.2.6 or later and that a Mobile Pro licence is assigned to you; the vendor says the app is available only with the relevant licences.
  2. On the device, sign in to Google Play and install ShireSystem Mobile PRO by Elecosoft (package co.uk.shiresystems.pirana); it is a free download and the licence is checked at login.
  3. Open the app and enter the server address, username and password your administrator gives you. If your organisation uses Entra ID single sign-on, that needs ShireSystem V4.5 or later on the server.
  4. Set the device's screen lock and ask your administrator whether work orders, documents and images are cached for offline use on your account, then test a work order with mobile data switched off and watch it sync when the signal returns.
  5. If your account uses barcode or QR sign-off, scan a real asset label and a stores label on the device; on the Tuga A6 check whether the built-in scan engine feeds the field or whether the app expects the camera.
  6. Turn on automatic app updates in Google Play, since Eleco supports only the two most current releases, and note the ShireSystem version your server runs so the app and server stay in step.

Questions

ShireSystem (formerly Pirana CMMS) and the Mobile Pro app on a Tuga device

The Google Play listing declares a minimum of Android 4.1, and the A10 (Android 14), A8 (Android 12) and A6 (Android 15) all run Google Play and are far above it. Whether the layout suits a 10.1 inch screen is not published: the listing shows a Phone chip and no Tablet chip, so trial it on the device you intend to buy and return it within 30 days if it is not right.

Yes, as far as the vendor's own materials show. Trade press from 2016 describes Pirana CMMS and its mobile apps from Shire Systems of Southampton, the Android app's package name is still co.uk.shiresystems.pirana, and the product is now sold as ShireSystem by Elecosoft UK Ltd, trading as Eleco. If your contract still says Pirana, ask your account manager which ShireSystem version you are on, because the app needs 3.2.6 or later.

The Play description says use on or offline and the iOS listing says assets can be tracked and maintained both online and offline. How much is cached and how conflicts are resolved is not published, so test it: open a work order with mobile data off, complete it, and watch it sync when you walk back into coverage.

The vendor says QR codes, barcodes and RFID tags are supported, without saying which RFID technology. Every Tuga device lists NFC, which reads 13.56MHz tags at a few centimetres; the W10's optional UHF RFID reader is a different, longer range technology. Ask Eleco which tag type your account expects before buying tags.

Only if someone needs the full browser client on site. Eleco wants the latest Chrome, Edge or Firefox, which the W10 runs on Windows 11 Pro, and its Ethernet port suits plant rooms without Wi-Fi. Engineers using Mobile Pro are better served by the Android devices, which cost £200 to £300 less.
